summary: 10-phase, ~15-hour implementation plan for the orchestrate-centric core consolidation. Phase 1 verifies the measured baseline and builds the audit-scope evidence roster; Phases 2-4 produce the Phase A design specification (A1-A7) ending in a completeness gate; Phases 5-6 assign exactly one verdict per audit-scope task across a design-coupled cluster and a remainder, closing with coverage arithmetic; Phase 7 reconciles verdicts, fixes the three sequencing-tension directions, finalizes the BLOCKING set, and emits an ordered backlog operation manifest; Phases 8-10 apply Phase C (create successors, revise/abandon/re-topic/backfill, then dependency ordering plus TODO regeneration and the VERIFICATION BAR closeout). The plan respects the meta-task boundary throughout: every phase's verification includes a git status --porcelain check that no path outside specs/ changed, and Phase 10 closes VERIFICATION BAR item 5 explicitly. The research dispatch-bypass finding was independently re-verified during planning and is carried as a first-class design input with a named post-collapse home and a rehome-before-deletion ordering constraint encoded as a dependency edge.

artifacts.summary: 10-phase plan covering the Phase A target-state design (A1-A7), the Phase B backlog audit, and the Phase C backlog operations; writes confined to specs/**.

memory_candidates.content: When planning a consolidation that promotes one component to sole entry point, verify what the promoted component actually does at its dispatch boundary before planning any deletion. In this codebase skill-orchestrate dispatches lifecycle agents via the Agent tool directly (subagent_type), bypassing the wrapping skills where Stage 4a memory retrieval and interactive --lit resolution exclusively live -- so the sole-entry-point collapse would have made a partial, silent capability loss total and permanent. The general pattern: a capability that lives in a wrapper layer rather than in the dispatched worker is invisible at the worker's own file and disappears when the wrapper is bypassed or deleted. Any plan that elevates a bypassing component must (a) enumerate the wrapper-only capabilities, (b) name a post-collapse home for each, and (c) encode a rehome-before-deletion ordering constraint as a real dependency edge, not as prose advice.
